newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - BHP Petroleum says can meet demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - BHP Petroleum says can meet demand.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday it was confident its petroleum division had enough oil and gas supplies to meet projected demand growth but said prices for these commodities were seen remaining flat this year.
Petroleum division profit for the year to May 31 slid 53.7 percent to A$329 million, including a write off of A$151 million for its investment in the Dai Hung oil field in Vietnam.
"Petroleum will continue to optimise the vale of its major oil and gas producing assets and accelerate the development of discovered reserves," BHP said in its 1995/96 annual report.

BHP's largest single source of group production and profits is the Bass Strait oil and gas complex, offshore south-east Australia, which is operated by joint venture partner and Exxon Corp subsidiary Esso Australia Ltd.
BHP has said it intends to continue infill drilling in Bass Strait to moderate the natural field decline
The North West Shelf Project was working towards boosting LNG production capabilities from the existing three trains, which produce 7.3 million tonnes a year, to five trains.
BHP also said it expected to build on promising early results from the Gulf of Mexico exploration by securing additional leases.
"The results of ongoing (global) exploration activity have enabled BHP Petroleum to add more reserves that it consumed in production (in 1995/96)," the company noted.

To complement growth from exploration, the unit was evaluating participating in countries where it was able to add value through project management expertise, financing capabilities and operational skills, BHP said.
